name: Anyin Morofo
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Anyin Morofo is not in the catalog. The sweep's single title hit, Carvalho 2015 'Accent et verbe en ibéro-roman', is a Glottolog computerized mis-assignment (lgcode set from the string 'phono' in the title); it concerns Ibero-Romance verb stress, not Anyi, and should be dropped from the per-language bibliography (Glottolog record saved as receipt). OpenAlex quota exhausted; Crossref has no record of the Carvalho work). The best first-hand stress statement remains the one already on file from the earlier audit: Delafosse 1900 pp.115-117, an explicit vowel-quality-sensitive accent rule (penult default; final if final vowel a/o; antepenult with penult e/u/i; prefix a- unaccented), which denies tone; later native-speaker work (Koffi 1990-2022) establishes a two-tone system with contours and treats Anyi as between tone, pitch-accent and accent types without giving a stress-position rule. Still unobtained and worth acquiring: Quaireau 1978 (thèse Nancy II) pp.217-8 and Quaireau 1987 (thèse d'État, Grenoble III, on the Moronou/Ndénié/Bona parlers), Burmeister 1983 'L'agni' in Atlas des langues kwa I. bib/.html,.

earlier_scan.note: only Ntumy & Boafo 2002 (SIL survey/subclassification) named on Glottolog; nothing describing Morofo stress found

new_statements.quote: Il y a en agni un accent, mais il ne se fait que faiblement sentir [...] Il n'y a pas en agni d'intonation musicale, comme il en existe [...] en yorouba [...] 1° L'accent est en général sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot [...] 2° L'accent est sur la dernière syllabe, si la voyelle de cette syllabe est un a [...] ou un o [...], à moins que l'avant-dernière syllabe n'ait aussi pour voyelle un a ou un o, auquel cas l'accent est sur la pénultième. [...] 3° Dans un mot d'au moins trois syllabes, si la voyelle de la pénultième est e, u ou i [...], l'accent est en général sur l'antépénultième. [...] 4° Les monosyllabes ne sont accentués que si l'on veut y attirer l'attention. 5° Le préfixe a [...] ne porte jamais l'accent.
new_statements.translation: There is an accent in Agni, but it is only weakly felt [...] There is no musical intonation in Agni such as exists [...] in Yoruba [...] 1. The accent is in general on the next-to-last syllable of the word [...] 2. The accent is on the last syllable if the vowel of that syllable is an a or an o, unless the penultimate syllable also has a or o as its vowel, in which case the accent is on the penult. [...] 3. In a word of at least three syllables, if the vowel of the penult is e, u or i [...], the accent is in general on the antepenult. [...] 4. Monosyllables are accented only if one wants to draw attention to them. 5. The prefix a- [...] never carries the accent.
new_statements.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1900. Essai de manuel de la langue agni parlée dans la moitié orientale de la Côte d'Ivoire. Paris: J. André, Librairie africaine et coloniale.
new_statements.locator: Cinquième partie, §I 'Accent', pp.115-116 (examples continue to p.117)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default penultimate accent, overridden by vowel quality (sonority): a low/open vowel a or o in the final syllable attracts the accent to the final unless the penult also has a/o; in trisyllables-plus a high/mid penult vowel (e, u, i) pushes accent to the antepenult, again unless a final a/o claims it (a preferred over o). Nominal/verbal prefix a- is never accented and is invisible to the count; monosyllables unaccented except under emphasis. Accent described as weak and independent of vowel length.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; in compounds of two nouns/verbs each member keeps its own accent (rule 6, p.116); enclitic-like particles (fwe, nu, su, nominaliser -re) count as the word's final syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: fro-ro 'cold' (penult accent despite final o); rule 2 'constant' for a but only 'general' for o; short o/a in the penult sometimes behave like e/u/i (rule 3).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent in citation forms (accented syllable italicised in examples). Author's data are Anyi in general, mainly Indénié and Bona areas with some Morofu (Koffi 2022:67); pre-tonological 1900 description. The modern Morofu-native description (Koffi 1990/2009, 2014, 2018, 2021, 2022; all saved) analyses Anyi Morofu as a two-tone language (H, L + HL, LH contours, downstep) with very low lexical functional load of tone, gives no stress position, but explicitly endorses Delafosse: 'All in all, Delafosse's insights about Anyi are accurate, and so is his characterization of the Anyi prosodic system' (Koffi 2022:67).
new_statements.identity_note: The only positional accent statement (Delafosse 1900) describes Anyi/Agni in general (language-level anyi1245), with data drawn mainly from the Indénié and Bona areas and only some from the Morofu area (Koffi 2022:67); Creissels & Kouadio 1977 allege some of his material is Baule. All the Morofo-specific descriptions (Koffi 1990/2009 dissertation, 2014, 2018 Guide, 2021, 2022; author is a native speaker of Anyi Morofu from the Bongouanou area) treat the variety as a two-tone language and give no stress position, though Koffi 2022 explicitly endorses Delafosse's prosodic characterization. A catalog entry for anyi1244 based on Delafosse should be flagged as inherited from the language-level description and as a 1900 pre-tonological account.

new_statements.quote: Il y a en agni un accent, mais il ne se fait que faiblement sentir [...] Il n'y a pas en agni d'intonation musicale, comme il en existe en certaines langues africaines, en yorouba (ou nago) par exemple. [...] 1° L'accent est en général sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot [...] 2° L'accent est sur la dernière syllabe, si la voyelle de cette syllabe est un a [...] ou un o [...], à moins que l'avant-dernière syllabe n'ait aussi pour voyelle un a ou un o, auquel cas l'accent est sur la pénultième. [...] 3° Dans un mot d'au moins trois syllabes, si la voyelle de la pénultième est e, û ou i [...], l'accent est en général sur l'antépénultième. [...] 5° Le préfixe a [...] ne porte jamais l'accent.
new_statements.translation: There is an accent in Agni, but it is only weakly perceptible [...] Agni has no musical intonation such as exists in some African languages, e.g. Yoruba (Nago). [...] 1. The accent is generally on the penultimate syllable of the word [...] 2. The accent is on the final syllable if its vowel is a or o, unless the penult also has a or o, in which case the accent is on the penult. [...] 3. In a word of at least three syllables, if the penult vowel is e, u or i, the accent is generally on the antepenult. [...] 5. The prefix a- never bears the accent.
new_statements.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1900. Essai de manuel de la langue agni parlée dans la moitié orientale de la Côte d'Ivoire. Paris: J. André. Cinquième partie, §I 'Accent', pp. 115-117.
new_statements.locator: pp. 115-116 (rules 1-3 and 5; section runs to p. 117 with rule 6 examples)
new_statements.reading: Weak, vowel-quality-sensitive word accent: default penult; final if the final vowel is a/o (a beats o) unless the penult also has a/o; antepenult in 3+-syllable words whose penult is e/u/i; monosyllables and the noun/verb prefix a- unaccented; compounds keep each member's accent. Delafosse denies lexical tone, which later work (Koffi 1990, 2014, 2018, 2022; Quaireau 1982) refutes: Anyi has two level tones H/L plus HL/LH contours. Koffi 2022 (Linguistic Portfolios 11:67), a native Anyi Morofu speaker, nevertheless calls Delafosse's characterization of the prosodic system 'accurate' and classifies Anyi as straddling tone / pitch-accent / accent types, with F0, intensity and duration all cueing grammatical moods, but gives no syllable-position rule for stress. Delafosse's data are Anyi in general, mainly Indénié/Bona with some Morofu (Koffi 2022:67), so this is the only positional stress rule on record for the language but is old, pre-tonal, and not dialect-specific. Not in catalog, so nothing to supersede; the item in this sweep (Carvalho 2015) contributes nothing.

sources.quote: Il y a en agni un accent, mais il ne se fait que faiblement sentir [...] Il n'y a pas en agni d'intonation musicale, comme il en existe [...] en yorouba [...] 1° L'accent est en général sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot [...] 2° L'accent est sur la dernière syllabe, si la voyelle de cette syllabe est un a [...] ou un o [...], à moins que l'avant-dernière syllabe n'ait aussi pour voyelle un a ou un o, auquel cas l'accent est sur la pénultième. sources.locator: Cinquième partie, §I 'Accent', pp.115-116 (examples continue to p.117)
sources.note: Explicit accent rules for Anyi (in general): accent weak but present; default on the penult; on the final syllable if its vowel is a or o unless the penult also has a/o; in words of 3+ syllables with penult e/u/i, on the antepenult (but a/o in the final wins); monosyllables unaccented unless emphasised; prefix a- never accented and not counted; compounds keep each member's accent. 'Il n'y a pas en agni d'intonation musicale, comme... en yorouba.' Data mostly Indénié/Bona with some Morofu (per Koffi 2022:67).

sources.citation: Koffi, Ettien. 2022. The chinks in the prosodic classification of languages: what kind of a tone language is Anyi? Linguistic Portfolios 11: 66-82 (art. 5). St. Cloud State University.
sources.note: Native-speaker linguist of Anyi MOROFU. Argues Anyi 'straddles' tone / pitch-accent / accent typologies: two tones but only ~74 tonal minimal pairs/triplets in 4,539 words (RFL 1.63%), verb tone fully predictable, F0 and duration (not just pitch) encode grammatical moods ('with regard to duration, Anyi behaves like a true accent language'). Quotes Delafosse 1900:115-117 in translation and states 'All in all, Delafosse's insights about Anyi are accurate, and so is his characterization of the Anyi prosodic system' (p.67). Gives no syllable position for word stress.

sources.citation: Koffi, Ettien. 2021. An acoustic phonetic analysis of three tonally contrastive grammatical moods in Anyi: orthographic implications. Linguistic Portfolios 10: 52-74.
sources.note: Anyi Morofu, 10 speakers; F0, intensity, duration of declarative/intentional/injunctive moods on subject pronoun and first TBU of verb. No word-stress position statement.

sources.note: pp.179-180: Anyi Morofou 'tonal structure is as follows: two High and Low level tones and two High-Low and Low-High contour tones. Anyi has downstep, downdrift... Tone is contrastive lexically and grammatically', followed by list of tonal minimal pairs. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Koffi, Ettien N'da. 1990 [revised and expanded 2009]. The interface between phonology and morpho(phono)logy in the standardization of Anyi orthography. PhD dissertation, Indiana University (2009 version, 221 pp., posted at orthographyclearinghouse.org).
sources.note: Anyi Morofou-based phonology/orthography. §1.2.3 Tone (p.19): 'Anyi has two level tones: High and Low. There are two contour tones: High-Low and Low-High. Tones have lexical differentiation functions in nouns. They have grammatical functions in verbal stems.' Ch.2 syllable structure, §2.9 tone marking; ch.5 loan phonology (French final-accented open syllables borrowed with vowel lengthening + HL). No section or statement on word stress (grep stress/accent/prominence nil apart from loanword remark).
